es.summary: La buprenorfina es un agonista parcial del receptor µ que se usa para el trastorno por uso de opioides y para analgesia moderada‑severa.
key_points: Agonista parcial: produce analgesia con techo de depresión respiratoria.
Alta afinidad por el receptor µ, desplazando agonistas completos.
Se combina con naloxona para evitar inyección intravenosa.
Efectos adversos comunes: estreñimiento, náuseas, somnolencia.
Interacciones importantes con depresores del SNC y CYP3A4.

mechanism: Se une al receptor µ con alta afinidad pero lo activa parcialmente.
Reduce la actividad de agonistas completos, disminuyendo cravings.
Produce analgesia y efecto techo en depresión respiratoria.
indications: Tratamiento del trastorno por uso de opioides (Mantenimiento).
Manejo del dolor moderado a severo cuando se requiere agonista parcial.
Prevención de recaídas en pacientes en desintoxicación.
contraindications: Insuficiencia respiratoria aguda o depresión respiratoria severa.
adverse_effects: Síndrome de abstinencia precipitado al suspender abruptamente (serious).
interactions: Depresores del SNC (benzodiacepinas, alcohol) aumentan riesgo de depresión respiratoria.
Inhibidores potentes de CYP3A4 (ketoconazol, eritromicina) aumentan niveles plasmáticos.
Inductores de CYP3A4 (rifampicina) pueden reducir eficacia.
Otros opioides pueden potenciar efectos sedantes.
nursing_care: Evaluar nivel de conciencia y frecuencia respiratoria antes de administrar.
Monitorizar presión arterial, pulso y saturación de O2 cada 2 h.
Observar signos de depresión respiratoria (RR < 12 rpm, SpO2 < 92%).
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen signos de intoxicación.
Mantener acceso venoso y naloxona a mano para reversión.
Revisar historial de alergias y medicamentos concomitantes.
patient_teaching: Tomar la dosis sublingual sin masticar ni tragar.
No inyectar ni compartir el medicamento.
Evitar alcohol y sedantes mientras esté en tratamiento.
Informar signos de sobredosis: respiración lenta, somnolencia excesiva.
No interrumpir el tratamiento sin consultar al profesional de salud.
Almacenar fuera del alcance de niños y mascotas.
antidote_overdose: Naloxona 0.4‑2 mg IV/IM, repetir cada 2‑3 min según respuesta.
Continuar monitorizando respiración y presión arterial después de la reversión.
Mantener soporte respiratorio y oxígeno suplementario si es necesario.

outcomes: Nivel de conciencia dentro de rango normal (alerta u orientado) en 24 h
Saturación de oxígeno ≥ 92 % sin asistencia en 24 h

interventions.action: Monitorizar frecuencia respiratoria y saturación de O2 cada 2 h
Evaluar nivel de conciencia usando escala de Glasgow cada 2 h
Mantener acceso venoso y tener naloxona disponible
interventions.rationale: Permitir intervención rápida en caso de sobredosis.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre uso correcto y riesgos de combinar con alcohol o benzodiacepinas
Revisar historial de medicamentos y posibles interacciones antes de administrar
Notificar al médico si RR < 12 rpm o SpO2 < 92 %
interventions.rationale: Garantizar intervención oportuna y ajuste de terapia.

en.summary: Buprenorphine is a partial µ receptor agonist used for opioid use disorder and moderate‑to‑severe pain.
key_points: Partial agonist: provides analgesia with a ceiling effect on respiratory depression.
High affinity for the µ receptor, displacing full agonists.
Combined with naloxone to deter intravenous injection.
Common adverse effects: constipation, nausea, drowsiness.
Important interactions with CNS depressants and CYP3A4.

mechanism: Binds to the µ receptor with high affinity but activates it partially.
Reduces activity of full agonists, decreasing cravings.
Provides analgesia and a ceiling effect on respiratory depression.
indications: Management of moderate to severe pain when a partial agonist is needed.
Prevention of relapse in patients undergoing detoxification.
contraindications: Acute respiratory insufficiency or severe respiratory depression.
interactions: CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, alcohol) increase risk of respiratory depression.
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin) raise plasma levels.
Other opioids can potentiate sedative effects.
nursing_care: Assess level of consciousness and respiratory rate before administration.
Monitor blood pressure, pulse, and O₂ saturation every 2 h.
Observe for signs of respiratory depression (RR < 12 rpm, SpO₂ < 92 %).
Hold the dose and notify the physician if signs of intoxication appear.
Maintain IV access and keep naloxone available for reversal.
Review allergy and concomitant medication history.
patient_teaching: Take the sublingual dose without chewing or swallowing.
Do not inject or share the medication.
Avoid alcohol and sedatives while on treatment.
Report overdose signs: slow breathing, excessive drowsiness.
Do not discontinue treatment without consulting a health professional.
Store out of reach of children and pets.
antidote_overdose: Naloxone 0.4‑2 mg IV/IM, repeat every 2‑3 min as needed.
Continue monitoring respiration and blood pressure after reversal.
Maintain respiratory support and supplemental oxygen if necessary.

outcomes: Level of consciousness within normal range (alert or oriented) within 24 h
O₂ saturation ≥ 92 % without assistance within 24 h

interventions.action: Monitor respiratory rate and O₂ saturation every 2 h
Assess level of consciousness using the Glasgow scale every 2 h
Maintain IV access and have naloxone available
interventions.rationale: Enable rapid intervention in case of overdose.

interventions.action: Educate patient on correct use and risks of combining with alcohol or benzodiazepines
Review medication history and potential interactions before administration
Notify physician if RR < 12 rpm or SpO₂ < 92 %
interventions.rationale: Ensure timely intervention and therapy adjustment.

key_points.1.quote: Buprenorphine has a high affinity for the opioid receptor and can displace other opioids that can cause opioid withdrawal to occur.

key_points.2.quote: The inclusion of naloxone with oral preparations of buprenorphine may seem nonsensical given that naloxone has poor oral bioavailability, but this is done to discourage intravenous abuse of buprenorphine, as the naloxone would cancel out the euphoric effects o

key_points.3.quote: The most common are gastrointestinal effects, including nausea, vomiting, and constipation.

key_points.5.quote: While naloxone rapidly reverses the effects of opioids within seconds to minutes, it only lasts approximately 20–30 minutes, which is less than the duration of action of many opioids.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Buprenorphine is a partial mu opioid receptor agonist that is designed to reduce the symptoms of opioid withdrawal and cravings in clients abstaining from opioid use.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression may occur with use of opioid agonists.

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: Opioid withdrawal occurs in clients using opioids for a chronic period who have abruptly discontinued the drug, or from rapid reversal of the drug’s effect with an opioid antagonist (e.g., naloxone).
